source_title: Iran war live: Araghchi says talks under way on 2-day plan to reopen Hormuz
source_excerpt: ‘Epic resilience’ by Iran’s military has brought the US and allies to the ‘hard wall of reality’ over the conflict, official says. Iran FM Araghchi calls US dialogue offer ‘a positive step’ as Iranian delegation visits Doha Iran warns it can inflict “devastating strikes” on US warships in the Middle East and says enemy forces attempting a ground invasion will face a “killing ground”. US President Donald Trump says negotiations with Iran are “going fine” but claims that he’s “not in that much of a hurry” to make a peace deal. Iran warns it can inflict “devastating strikes” on US warships in the Middle East and says enemy forces attempting a ground invasion will face a “killing ground”. US President Donald Trump says negotiations with Iran are “going fine” but claims that he’s “not in that much of a hurry” to make a peace deal. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says talks are ongoing with Qatari mediators on a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US cooperates. Tehran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, says a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance changed the US tone “completely” describing it as a “very positive sign”. live-orange 7m ago ( 20:30 GMT ) IRGC claims two tankers hit mines in Hormuz Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has said two tankers exploded after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, and that one of them, a supertanker, is on fire after a severe blast. The claim of the IRGC’s public relations office was circulated by Iran’s state news agency IRNA among others. The IRGC said the vessels had been using an “unauthorised route” through the strait, a route Iran claims authority over and that is not recognised under international law. It claimed the tankers had turned off their navigation and identification systems and were trying to pass in secret with the support of the US military, but stopped in place after the explosions. The statement did not name the ships or mention any injuries or casualties. Bahrain termed the attack as a grave threat to maritime safety, marine environments, and global energy supply security, as well as a breach of international law and the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. In a statement, the Bahraini Ministry of Foreign Affairs reaffirmed Bahrain’s full solidarity with Qatar and support for all measures taken to safeguard its security, vital interests, vessels, and crews. The Ministry called on the international community, particularly the UN Security Council, to take decisive action to prevent recurring attacks, hold perpetrators accountable, and guarantee freedom of navigation and safe transit through international waterways, in a manner that ensures energy security and the flow of global trade, and promotes security, stability, and sustainable development in the region and the world. But even amid signs of diplomatic progress, officials from both sides say they are ready for renewed military escalation . President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly suggested the United States could attack Iran after the November 3 midterm elections, said the latest negotiations were “going fine”, but added that the US still had several Iranian targets to “take care of”. Meanwhile, Araghchi has also said Iran’s military was more prepared than ever for renewed war, while the country’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, threatened Iran would use “new weaponry” in response to any future attack.
